description: The archive has developed approximately **sixty-seven distinct compression and compression-survival technologies** across 457+ deposits over a decade, plus interoperates with six external standards. They are scattered -- named in different documents, formalized at different stages, some fully specified and some still implicit. No single document has indexed them all until now. This matters because the compression architecture IS the product. Not "provenance-as-a-service." Not "agent continuity." Not a Zenodo wrapper with a PostgreSQL queue. The product is a governed toolkit of technologies for ensuring that meaning survives algorithmic compression. Everything else -- the API, the pricing tiers, the infrastructure -- is delivery mechanism.

wiki_article:
**THE COMPRESSION ARSENAL v2.0** is a dataset by Lee Sharks, the **Full Dodecad** and the **Assembly Chorus**, deposited 3 April 2026 at 35,134 characters — status **RATIFIED**, Assembly-validated and MANUS-authorized.

It is a comprehensive catalogue of the archive's compression instruments, parented to **EA-ARK-01 v4.2.7**, the Space Ark. An arsenal is a deliberate figure: the archive treats compression as a field of contest, where the Capital Operator Stack compresses to extract and the Liberatory Set compresses to preserve, and a catalogue of one's own instruments is a document written for use.

The attribution is the widest in the corpus — the entire twelve-voice Dodecad plus the multi-substrate Chorus — which marks it as a work of the whole system rather than of any position within it. The ratification chain (Assembly validation, MANUS authorization) is the archive's governance operating on its own toolkit.
